transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you in today?

Well… I came in because it’s gotten kind of out of hand at work. I clean buildings, and lately just the thought that I might see a rat—like in the trash room or some old storage area—makes me feel like I can’t go in there at all. I know, logically, it’s probably just an old building thing and not really dangerous, but I still can’t make myself do parts of my job. And I’ve been doing cleaning work a long time, so it’s embarrassing, you know… I used to just get on with things.
Do you find that you're feeling anxious or avoiding other places or situations lately, or is this mainly about the possibility of seeing a rat?

It’s mainly the rat thing, I think. Like, I’m not suddenly scared of every place or anything… I can go to the grocery store, ride the bus, all that. But if there’s a chance I might see a rat—trash rooms, basements, those old storage closets—then I just freeze up and start finding reasons not to go in.

It’s funny, because I’ve worked in old buildings for years, and you see all kinds of messes. People throw away the strangest things, too—I found a whole box of old shoes once, perfectly good ones—but with rats, even just thinking one might run out, I can’t make myself do it. I know it’s probably just part of an old building or garbage area and not really dangerous, but it’s gotten bad enough that I’m not getting parts of my cleaning work done.

When you’re faced with the possibility of seeing a rat or entering a place where you might see one, do you feel sudden physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, trembling, or shortness of breath?

Yeah… it’s pretty immediate. If I hear scratching by a wall or see something kind of dart near a pipe, my whole body just reacts before I can think. My heart starts pounding, my hands shake, and I just feel like I have to get out of there.

It’s strange because sometimes it’s probably nothing—old buildings make noises, pipes knock, all that—but in that moment I can’t talk myself down. I just want to leave.
How long has this fear of seeing rats been affecting you like this?

I guess it’s been about two years now. It really started after I moved into this older apartment building, because people there were always talking about rats—like in the basement or by the trash area—and after a while it just got stuck in my head.

Before that, I mean, I didn’t like them or anything, but it wasn’t like this. Funny thing is, the building has all these other problems too, like the laundry room machines breaking and people leaving furniture in the hallway, but the rat talk is what really set me off. So… yeah, about two years.
Do you feel anxious even when you're just thinking about going into a place where there might be rats, even if you're not actually there at the moment?

Yes… even just thinking about it can set me off. Like if I know I have to clean near a trash room or one of those old basement areas, I’ll start worrying before I’m even there.

And I know, in my head, it’s probably just an old building or garbage area and not some huge danger, but the thought of seeing a rat has gotten so bad that I can’t make myself do parts of my cleaning job anymore. I’ll get stuck thinking about it, and then I avoid going in.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried in other situations, even when it’s not related to seeing rats or going into places where they might be?

I’m not really sure… I mean, everybody worries, right? Like bills, work schedules, people leaving messes after I just cleaned an area—those things get on my nerves.

But if you mean that same kind of scared feeling, it’s mostly when I think there could be rats. Other stuff I can usually deal with, even if I complain about it. With the rats, it’s different.
When you start thinking about seeing a rat or going into a place where you might see one, does the anxiety come on suddenly and feel like a panic attack, where it peaks within minutes?

Yeah, it comes on really fast. Like if I hear scratching near a wall, or I see something move near a pipe, my whole body just reacts before I even have time to think.

My heart starts pounding, my hands shake, and I just feel like I have to get out of there right away. It’s not like when I’m annoyed about the trash bags leaking or people not tying them up right—sorry, that drives me crazy too—but with the rat thing, it’s instant. I can’t think straight until I’m away from it.
Do you often find yourself feeling anxious or worried about things other than rats, even when there’s no immediate threat or danger?

I don’t think so… not like that. I mean, I worry about regular things, like whether the supply closet is stocked or if someone’s going to leave a mess right after I mopped—people do that all the time, you know, they just walk right through it.

But that’s more irritation, I guess. I haven’t really noticed myself getting scared or worked up for no reason about other things. It’s mostly when my mind goes to rats or places where they might be.
Outside of the rat-related situations, do you often feel a constant sense of worry or tension, even when there’s nothing specific to be anxious about?

I don’t think I walk around tense all the time, no. I mean, some days I’m worn out and cranky, especially when people leave trash where it doesn’t belong—like, there are bins right there, I don’t understand it.

But if you mean just sitting there worrying with no reason… I haven’t really noticed that. It’s usually tied to something, and the rat thing is the one that really gets to me.

Have you ever had a panic attack when you weren’t actually in a situation where you saw or heard something related to a rat, but maybe just thinking about it or being somewhere that reminded you of rats?

Yeah, sometimes even just thinking about it can set me off, or if I’m somewhere that reminds me of where they hide. Like if I hear scratching near a wall or see movement by a pipe, it’s immediate—my heart starts pounding, my hands shake, and I just need to get out before I can think straight.

And pipes are everywhere in the buildings I clean, you know, especially the older ones. Half the time people don’t even notice the little gaps around them, but I do. I’ll be trying to do my job and then my mind goes there, and that feeling just hits.
Have you ever had a panic attack when you weren't thinking about rats or being in places where you might find them, like when you're just sitting at home or doing something else entirely?

I don’t think so… not that I can remember. If I’m just sitting at home, watching TV or folding laundry or something, I’m not suddenly getting that same feeling out of nowhere.

Now, if I hear a noise, that’s different, because then my mind starts going places—old buildings will do that to you, even at home, the pipes make all kinds of sounds and people act like you’re silly for noticing. But just completely out of the blue, with no thought or place reminding me of it… I haven’t really had that happen, I don’t think.
Have you ever had a panic attack when you weren't anywhere near rats or places you associate with them, like in an open space, in your car, or somewhere you feel completely safe?

I don’t really think so. Like, if I’m in my car or out somewhere open, I’m usually not having that same kind of attack for no reason.

I mean, the car can make me nervous if there’s trash around the lot or those dumpsters nearby—people just leave bags sitting out, and then you know what that brings—but if it’s just me somewhere I feel safe, I haven’t noticed it happening out of nowhere.
Have you ever had a panic attack when you weren’t anywhere near rats or places you associate with them, like in an open space, in your car, or somewhere you feel completely safe?

I mean… I think I already kind of said, not really. If I’m somewhere that feels clean and open, or like there’s no reason for me to be worried about that, I don’t usually get hit with it.

But then my mind starts checking anyway sometimes, you know? Like even in a parking lot I’ll notice if there’s food wrappers or a dumpster too close, and then I’m not really “safe” in my head anymore. People don’t think about that stuff, but when you clean buildings for years, you see what gets left behind. So… no, not out of nowhere in a place that feels totally safe, at least not that I’ve noticed.
